title: Herb Scissors Cleaning Comb Tricks for Sticky Basil
meta_description: Discover proven herb scissors cleaning comb tricks for sticky basil, keep your five‑blade shears fresh, and enjoy flawless chopping every time.
html:
When basil gets sticky from its natural oils, even the best herb scissors can jam. The secret isn’t a fancy dishwasher cycle—it’s the cleaning comb that comes with the Herb Scissors. Below are practical, step‑by‑step tricks for using that comb to keep your five‑blade herb shears cutting cleanly, whether you’re mincing cilantro, chives, or basil.

Why Basil Sticks and How It Affects Your Scissors

Basil’s aromatic leaves are coated with a thin layer of essential oils. When you snip a handful, those oils release and quickly cling to the metal blades. The result? Blades that feel gummy, lose their precision, and eventually rust if not cleaned promptly. This is why the herb scissors cleaning comb basil technique matters more than a quick rinse.

Step‑One: The Quick Rinse (What to Do Immediately After Cutting)

Before you reach for the comb, give the blades a swift rinse under warm running water. Warm water loosens the sticky residue, and a gentle stream prevents the oils from drying onto the metal. Avoid using harsh detergents; a mild dish soap applied sparingly is enough.

Step‑Two: Using the Cleaning Comb Effectively

The cleaning comb that ships with the Herb Scissors is a tiny, stainless‑steel brush designed to slip between the five blades. Here’s how to get the most out of it:

  1. Hold the scissors open: Pinch the handles together just enough to keep the blades spread.
  2. Insert the comb: Slide the comb’s teeth into the gap between each blade, starting at the base where the blades meet the handle.
  3. Scrub gently: Move the comb back and forward a few times. The fine teeth scrape away any remaining basil oil without dulling the cutting edges.
  4. Rinse again: Run the scissors under water to wash away the dislodged residue.
  5. Dry thoroughly: Pat the blades dry with a clean kitchen towel or let them air‑dry on a rack.

Doing this routine after each use keeps the blades sharp and prevents the build‑up that can turn a fresh batch of cilantro into a clumpy mess.

Step‑Three: Deep Cleaning for Stubborn Build‑Up

If you notice a film after a few weeks of use, give the scissors a deeper clean:

  • Fill a small bowl with warm, soapy water (a drop of dish soap is sufficient).
  • Submerge the scissors for 2‑3 minutes.
  • Use the cleaning comb while the blades are still wet to dislodge any hardened oil.
  • Rinse thoroughly and dry immediately.

For extra protection, you can wipe the blades with a dab of food‑grade mineral oil after drying. This creates a barrier against moisture and prolongs the life of your herb scissors.

Maintenance Habits That Extend the Life of Your Herb Scissors

Beyond the comb, a few everyday habits make a big difference:

Store them dry and separated. Keep the scissors in a utensil drawer with the blades open, or hang them on a magnetic strip. This prevents accidental contact with other metal tools that could nick the edges.

Avoid cutting frozen herbs. Frozen basil releases more moisture, which can freeze onto the blades and cause corrosion.

Use them only for herbs. The five‑blade design excels at fine chopping. Trying to cut tougher vegetables can bend the blades, making cleaning harder and reducing precision.

When to Replace Your Herb Scissors

Even with diligent cleaning, metal fatigue happens. If you notice any of the following, it’s time to consider a new pair:

  • One or more blades are visibly dull or bent.
  • The comb no longer reaches between the blades because the spacing has widened.
  • Rust appears despite regular drying.

Because the Herb Scissors are built with stainless steel, they usually last several years with proper care. Replacing them only when performance drops ensures you always have a reliable tool for basil, cilantro, chives, and more.

FAQ

Can I wash the cleaning comb in the dishwasher?

Yes, the comb is dishwasher‑safe, but a quick hand wash with warm, soapy water is faster and prevents the comb from bouncing around and possibly damaging the scissor blades.

Is the cleaning comb safe for all types of herb scissors?

The comb is designed specifically for the five‑blade Herb Scissors. It fits snugly between those blades; using it on different scissors may not reach all the gaps effectively.

Do I need to oil the blades after each cleaning?

Oiling isn’t required after every wash, but a light coating of food‑grade mineral oil once a month helps maintain smooth operation and protects against rust.
